name: Silk
notes: Atlanta quintet produced by Keith Sweat — the explicit-slow-jam end of the new jack swing tail, 1992–1999. The research gives "61–90; ballads 61–72 with the backbeat on 3", so the ballad band is the base: 61–72 felt, `halfTime` true, snare `halftime_3`. Three drum deltas come from the board description: "soft kick on 1" at one or two hits a bar with the genre's syncopation nearly off, "shaker on offbeat 8ths" as a dedicated offbeat perc lane at two to four hits a bar rather than a hat pattern, and a hat lane cut to an 8th base at 0.05 fill density because the swung 16th hat is stated to appear "only in the uptempo cuts". Harmony is "minor-7th/9th vamps" under "five-part harmony with a high falsetto lead", so the seventh and ninth shares carry 0.86 between them and the melody register is the highest in this batch. "Long held notes, low note-density, melisma only on the tag" is the 2–5 density, the legato articulation and the empty-bar bias. The bass is "sustained synth bass on the root, mixed loud, no sub articulation" — a single-degree cell at a 0.97 root follow, and no `bass808` block. ⚠ Confidence is **low** because the research rates this entry medium-low and says so explicitly: only the tempo points and the producer identity are sourced, and the drum and harmony detail is marked `[LOW-CONF, board-level]` — it is Keith Sweat's grammar applied to this group, not a name-specific reading. The key claim is likewise `[LOW-CONF]`, so the keys are lane-level. ⚠ Every velocity, density and register number here is INFERRED. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 941/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.2 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. Second, `countermelody.densityRatio` became a range, [0.22, 0.45], rather than a flat 0.22. That parameter decides how many notes the part has at all, and at 0.22 it was two or three; a part that short has almost no shapes to be distinct in. The low end is kept because it is the thin reading the entry's texture implies, and it is now the bottom of a band rather than the only answer — so how much of the lead the pad answers varies take to take. ⚠ Every value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "five-part harmony with a high falsetto lead over minor-7th/9th vamps; long held notes, low note-density, melisma only on the tag.", and every claim in it still holds after the change. ⚠ **And the style pool was opened.** `generators::counter` can play five answer shapes and this block asked for one. `answer_lick` is added because the entry names it — "five-part harmony with a high falsetto lead over minor-7th/9th vamps; long held notes, low note-density — spoken intro, 8-bar verse, harmony chorus, extended ad-lib vamp-out that is longer than the verse" — and the vamp is the `sustain_pad` the block already had; the ad-lib vamp-out that runs longer than the verse is a second voice answering the lead in its gaps, which is `answer_lick`. ⚠ The weights are INFERRED; the layer they weight is not.
